name: TsumuKey
subtitle: One keyboard, all your languages.
description:
An iOS keyboard for people who type in several languages at once. Pick any two of English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese: suggestions and corrections mix them, with no switching. Turn on Detect Language to list them all; the keyboard follows the two you're typing. Japanese is always there: type romaji and tap the chip, or use the kana flick pad.

Predictions and corrections run on your phone; the keyboard never goes online.

After installing: Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards → Add New Keyboard → TsumuKey, then turn on Allow Full Access so the keyboard can read the app's settings and models.

versions.localizedDescription: Italian and Portuguese. Detect Language: list several languages and the keyboard follows the two you're typing. Korean keyboards (Dubeolsik and Cheonjiin) with touch-aware autocorrect. Long-press a suggestion for a grid of alternatives. Punctuation waits for a space before attaching. Emoji in the suggestion bar.
Fix for SideStore and AltStore installs: the keyboard now follows the app's settings (languages, colours) instead of its defaults.
Faster next-word suggestions; swapped letters corrected (wrold → world); French accents on one-letter words (a → à); Japanese keyboard can be turned off; nine layouts; maths and currency in the bar.
